definitions.explanation: A large white crane with black neck and wing feathers and a patch of bare red skin on its crown. In Japan it lives mainly in eastern Hokkaido and is a protected species and a symbol of long life.

examples.japanese: {丹頂鶴|たんちょうづる}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{飛|と}んでいる→飛ぶ：00759_tobu⟧。
⟦{北海道|ほっかいどう}→北海道：11010_hokkaidou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{丹頂鶴|たんちょうづる}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw red-crowned cranes in Hokkaido.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{釧路湿原|くしろしつげん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{丹頂鶴|たんちょうづる}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{雪|ゆき}→雪：00584_yuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{踊|おど}る→踊る：01250_odoru⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{求愛|きゅうあい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In the winter Kushiro Marshes, red-crowned cranes court each other as if dancing in the snow.

notes:
Often just {丹頂|たんちょう}. {丹|たん} is red and {頂|ちょう} is the top of the head, naming the red crown.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The crane is a traditional symbol of long life and good fortune (⟦{鶴|つる}→鶴：04359_tsuru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{千年|せんねん}、⟦{亀|かめ}→亀：02198_kame⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{万年|まんねん}→万年：28146_mannen⟧), and the red-crowned crane is the one pictured on New Year cards, wedding kimono, and the old 1,000-yen note.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {丹頂鶴|たんちょうづる}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{求愛|きゅうあい}⟦ダンス→ダンス：03856_dansu⟧: the courtship dance of the cranes
- {特別天然記念物|とくべつてんねんきねんぶつ}: special natural monument (its legal status)
